operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order's only command, to amend Subdivision VI of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules by adding paragraph 6, is a self-executing amendment that took effect on signing: the order states no other effective date, and its own signature line reads June 29, 1939. The command was therefore performed on issue, 1939-06-29 (actor: the President, Franklin D. Roosevelt; mechanism: performance of a self-executing amendment). The paragraph it inserted continued in the Rules only for the period it states is "ending June 30, 1940", and that period is a term of the inserted rule, not a continuing command of this order. No continuing predicate exists for 2026-10-14.

Under the authority vested in me by

when nominations and assignments of  
agricultural attaches, the selection or  
assignment of Foreign Service officers  
for specialized training in agricultural  
work, or other matters of interest to the  
Department of Agriculture are under  
consideration.

Commerce and the Department of Agri­
culture who shall be designated as  
members of the Board of Foreign Serv­
ice Personnel shall also be members of  
the School Board directing the Foreign  
Service Officers’  Training School, as es­
tablished and provided for by section 8  
of Executive Order No. 5642 of June 8,  
1931, which is hereby amended accord­
ingly, and each shall sit as a member of  
the School Board when matters of inter­
est to his respective Department shq.n  
be under consideration.
4. With reference to the Board of Ex­
aminers for the Foreign Service, the first  
paragraph of section 3 of the said Exec­
utive Order No. 5642 of June 8, 1931, is  
hereby amended to read as follows:
“3. Examination for the Foreign Serv­
ice. There is hereby constituted a Board  
of Examiners, which shall conduct ex­
aminations to determine the eligibility of  
candidates for the Foreign Service, com­
posed as follows: Three Assistant Sec­
retaries of State designated by the  
Secretary of State, an officer of the De­
partment of Commerce designated by  
the Secretary of Commerce and accept­
able to the Secretary of State, an officer  
of the Department of Agriculture des-  
!  ignated by the Secretary of Agriculture  
and acceptable to the Secretary of State,  
the Chief of the Division of Foreign  
Service Personnel, and the Chief Exam­
iner of the Civil Service Commission.

he deems it necessary, designate another  
officer of his Department to serve for  
him on the Board, provided such officer  
as may be designated to represent a  
member of the Board shall be acceptable  
to the Secretary of State and approved  
by him.
“The rules for the conduct of exam­
inations as established in subsections
(a) to (k), inclusive, of section 3 of the  
said Executive Order No. 5642 of June  
8, 1931, shall remain in full force and  
effect.”

July 1, 1939.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8187 (June 29, 1939; filed June 30, 1939) is a one-sentence amendment of the Civil Service Rules: that Subdivision VI of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules is amended by adding a paragraph (paragraph 6, excepting FBI positions other than fingerprint classifiers for the period July 1, 1939 to June 30, 1940). Its only command is that self-executing amendment, which was carried out when the order was issued. The order imposes no duty on any officer, sets no deadline for later action and revokes nothing, so no continuing command remained in the order itself after issue. What remained was the inserted paragraph 6 in the Rules, and by its own words that paragraph applied only for a period that began on July 1, 1939 and was "ending June 30, 1940" (recorded inclusively, so the exclusive reading ends the period as June 30, 1940 begins). The order's status was undecided and its status history is the single Office of the Federal Register catalog observation whose note text is empty, which establishes no current effect. The status is therefore judged from the order's own terms and the bounded searches: the order is not in force on 2026-10-14. Searching the held order texts for the paragraph's wording found later orders that re-amended paragraph 6 of Subdivision VI for later one-year periods; they amend the Rules text that this order inserted, not any command of this order, and none names Executive Order 8187 by number (no held text cites that number as a revoked, superseded or extended order).
